subject: Post-demo: Vendor truth table, decision criteria & follow-up experiments
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@northbridgehealth.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed bake-off truth table and experiments

Hi Sam / Elaine —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed set of follow-up experiments for the vendor bake-off so your decision team can compare apples-to-apples. I’ve attached an editable truth table plus a short POC plan.

Key pain points you emphasized
- Sensitive PHI throughput: many prompts contain patient context and you need guaranteed in-region processing + auditable logs.
- Tail latency for triage flows: SLA target is 150–200ms 95th for short prompts in production.
- Cost predictability at scale: monthly spend ceiling for ML inference pools.
- Output fidelity on structured discharge summaries (format + medical terminology).

Decision criteria (tentative, please confirm)
1) Security/compliance (in-region, SOC2 + encryption, KMS integration)
2) Latency SLO (95th and p95 tail behavior under mixed traffic)
3) Cost per 1k tokens at target concurrency / batching profile
4) Fidelity on 5 canonical prompt families (discharge summary, lab interpretation, patient Q&A, triage routing, billing code suggestion)
5) Operational controls: rollout policies, canary, fallback to cheaper model variant

Competitors in scope for the bake-off (what you told us)
- Vendor A (focused on managed endpoints)
- Vendor B (strong open-model offering, less mature private deployment)
- Redwood (our side) — we propose experiments below to expose practical differences.

Proposed experiments / truth-table rows (short description + why it matters)
- End-to-end in-region latency (5x short-prompt measurement at 1, 5, 20 concurrent clients): shows tail behavior under expected load.
- Prefix / KV cache delta: compare warm vs cold prefix caching on structured prompts; likely large cost/latency win for repetitive templates.
- Quantized model quality sweep (q4 -> q8): measures where fidelity drops for clinical terminology.
- Failure/fallback test: simulate a model OOM / region failover and validate automatic fallback correctness and latency penalty.
- Cost scaling: estimate tokens per month for production workload and run an emulation at 10k QPS-equivalent to measure cost telemetry.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Elaine: confirm final decision criteria and who will sign off (clinical lead + infra lead).
- Sam: share a redacted sample set (5 prompts x 5 variants each) for the fidelity tests by EOD Tue.
- Redwood (Aditya): we’ll instrument and share a pre-populated truth table and test harness by Tue EOD so vendors run identical workloads.

Tentative schedule
- May 18–21: vendors upload results + Redwood runs shared harness for parity tests
- May 24: internal scoring meeting at NBH to review truth table

Attachments: nbh-bakeoff-truth-table.xlsx (editable), redwood-poc-plan.pdf (test harness + sample scripts)

If this looks right I’ll lock the test definitions and ask vendors to run the harness next week.

Thanks,
Monica

Thanks Monica — this is excellent and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Decision makers: Clinical sign-off will be Dr. Priya Mehta (cc’d when needed), infra sign-off is Elaine. Procurement will weigh in if price delta > 18%.
2) For the fidelity tests, the priority prompts are: discharge summary (short), triage routing (multi-turn), and lab interpretation (structured). The billing code suggestion is lower priority.
3) On the failover test: can you confirm whether fallback is to a model variant in the same region before cross-region? We want to avoid cross-region PHI movement.

Sam

Looping in some technical detail on the test harness and what we need from NBH. Draft notes below — I’ll attach a short runner script and an example manifest.

What Redwood will supply (by Tue EOD):
- A Dockerized harness that replays your prompt set at configurable concurrency and records per-request latency, token counts, and HTTP error taxonomy.
- A prefilled truth-table with columns: vendor, model_variant, region, quantization, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens, failure_rate, fidelity_score (0-5), cost_estimate/month.
- A script to produce warm vs cold prefix measurements (10 sequential cold runs then warm runs with KV cache enabled).

What we need from NBH
- Redacted prompt set (5–10 canonical prompts) + expected output artifacts for fidelity scoring (JSON schema).
- Confirmation that all tests must run within US regions (no cross-region fallback unless explicitly requested).

Open technical questions
- Do you want us to keep the canary window for fallback at 60s or 120s? Shorter gives faster failover, longer reduces flapping; suggest 60s for triage flows.
- For quantization sweeps, do you want us to preserve int8 vs q4 comparisons? We can include both but it will add ~24 hours of vendor runs.

Attachments: redwood-test-harness-example.tar.gz (stub)

I’ll start building the manifest; Monica — once Sam/Elaine confirm the prompt set I’ll schedule a run and share a public Drive folder with raw outputs.

— Aditya
